static_findings: The RM-1085/RM-1116 service schematic separates iris sensor connector signals from platform flash signals.
The extracted FSTROBE/TORCH_EN/FLASH_EN and STROBE/TORCH/I2C/ENABLE labels are consistent with the separate rear Hill flash path; OCR wire geometry is unavailable, so this is not a net-level proof.

Windows qccamplatform8994 helper 0x42e560 is called from two camera configuration sites with selector arguments 0 and 1; its generic indirect I/O requests do not identify a Cityman TLMM pin or the CCI GPIO register base.
Linux MSM CCI GPIO write remains unsupported in the pinned source; the old ioctl has no payload for a timed sequence.
reason_stopped: The one-shot minimum-level emitter request was accepted and shut off cleanly. No camera was streamed during the pulse, so no frame synchronization result was collected. Windows CCI output-to-board routing and the CCI GPIO register/IRQ/timing contract remain unresolved; no kernel build or temporary boot was justified by this test.

phone_test.scope: iris camera ID 2 preview with one minimum-level IR pulse and user-visible Yes/No observation prompt
phone_test.result: One app-triggered minimum-level pulse: Camera2 IR_ANALYZE frame 80 completed at 29.995718 ms, ISO 100 while pulseSequenceActive=true. Matching 1920x1080 YUV callback had the same sensor timestamp and arrived at the helper OFF acknowledgement. User selected Yes and reported seeing faint red glow. Pixels were discarded; no optical output/safety or image-quality conclusion.
phone_test.cleanup: Feedback app force-stopped; Active Camera Clients returned []; torch_0, torch_1, flash_0, flash_1 all read 0; temporary helper files and ADB forward removed.
phone_test.limits: No frame pixels exported, no eye-region quality or matcher check, and no optical/IR test.

installed_android_biometric_state.interpretation: The installed OS has no iris biometric sensor registration; local framework patches are not active on this build.

setup_photo_review.visual_assessment: Phone is beneath a white paper canopy/tunnel. The photographed interior appears matte and diffuse; no metal can or obvious mirror-like surface appears in the pictured path.
setup_photo_review.limits: A photo cannot establish material reflectance, complete beam geometry, or whether people/animals are outside the photographed area.

emitter_test.scope: one bounded minimum-level torch_0 pulse directed into the pictured paper diffuser
emitter_test.result_limit: Confirms the helper accepted and stopped the minimum-level software request; it does not establish LED optical output, exposure safety, or camera synchronization.

interactive_feedback_test.scope: one user-requested minimum-level torch_0 pulse while only iris camera ID 2 was open
interactive_feedback_test.pulse_helper: app UI displayed the feedback question only after receiving ON and OFF-confirmed helper replies
interactive_feedback_test.user_observation: User selected Yes; app UI and log recorded faint red glow seen from the front IR LED.
interactive_feedback_test.preview: The iris preview had delivered 1122 capture-result callbacks before it was closed. No normal front-camera client was active.
interactive_feedback_test.limits: This confirms one successful software-timed pulse/capture sequence and one user-visible glow report. It does not quantify IR optical output, safety, repeatability, or image usefulness; the YUV pixels were discarded.
interactive_feedback_test.cleanup: Feedback app force-stopped; active camera clients returned []; temporary helper and adb forward removed; torch_0, torch_1, flash_0, flash_1 read 0.

capture_result.analysis_note: The app received the matching YUV image and ran its in-memory analysis path; its detailed spatial-luma/eye diagnostic is shown only in the private UI and was not recovered before force-stop.

helper_timing.note: Software/helper timestamps, not measured optical on-time.
